Alexandra M.: Hey @people-ops quick question — my due date is May 20 and I’m planning to start parental leave June 1. Our performance cycle ends May 31. Will being on leave affect my bonus proration or promotion consideration? 
Priya (People Ops): Congrats! :tada: Short answer: being on approved parental leave does not automatically disqualify you from promotion. For bonuses, it depends on payroll/bonus rules — if you’re on unpaid leave during part of the bonus period we may prorate. Can you share your expected leave dates and whether any of it will be unpaid?
Alexandra M.: Thanks — planning for 12 weeks total, 8 paid (company top‑up) then 4 unpaid. All continuous starting June 1.
Priya (People Ops): OK. Policy highlights: 1) Bonus eligibility is based on active employment at payout and the % of the bonus year you were on paid payroll. 2) For company‑toppped paid leave we treat you as paid for proration. 3) Unpaid weeks will reduce the prorated portion unless you opt into an alternate approval (we can escalate). Promotions: your manager and calibration committee evaluate contributions during the review window; approved leave itself isn’t a bar.
Sean R.: I’ll include Alex in calibration. Please prepare the usual calibration packet and note the leave dates so comp team sees it. I support promotion consideration based on Q1–Q2 work.
Maya (Payroll): Payroll/process notes: we need the LOA code in Workday before the payroll cutoff (submit LOA 2 pay periods before leave start). For the bonus: payroll runs eligibility report on June 15 for payouts on July 1 (example dates). If LOA is coded as paid (company_topup = yes) those weeks count as paid for proration. If unpaid, we calculate: prorated_bonus = full_bonus * (months_paid / 12).
Alexandra M.: Good to know. If unpaid weeks lower my prorated %, is there an appeal?
Priya (People Ops): Yes — we have a compensation exception process for parental leaves with mitigating circumstances. It’s discretionary and needs manager + People Ops signoff before the comp cycle is locked. Please submit the "compensation_exception" form and mark it urgent. Link: https://intranet.redwood.com/hr/comp-exceptions (internal).
Priya (People Ops): Action items for you: 1) Submit parental leave request in Workday this week. 2) Check the box for company top‑up (if eligible). 3) Ask Sean to attach your calibration packet and recommend promotion if appropriate. 4) If you want to pursue exception, fill the comp-exception form ASAP.
Sean R.: I’ll attach the packet and add a short endorsement. Alex — I’ll ping you tomorrow to review. :thumbsup:
Maya (Payroll): One more: if the bonus is discretionary and you were active for >=9 months (or equivalent paid months) we usually pay at 100% per policy; between 6–9 months we prorate; below 6 months may be ineligible depending on the plan. I can check exact plan rules after you file LOA.
hr-bot: Reminder — Workday LOA submission deadline is 2025-05-18 (automated reminder).
Alexandra M.: Awesome — thank you all. I’ll submit LOA today and start the comp-exception form just in case. Appreciate the help!
